shadow.$description: Semantic shadow aliases. v0.11.13 — every accent-coloured shadow now references the spring-green {color.alpha.accent.*} primitives. Pre-v0.11.13 the focus rings, button glows, ai-shimmer, input focus + success halos all hardcoded v0.4 lime rgba(74,222,128,X) and so silently bypassed the v0.11 brand recolor. With this rewiring, any future accent retune cascades through every shadow alias automatically. Input.error references {color.alpha.danger.32} (refined v0.11 #E5484D) so the error halo inherits the danger primitive — pre-v0.11.13 it was inlined at the v0.10 #ef4444 RGB.

card.$description: Cards default to a hairline border with this very subtle shadow. Reach for shadow.lifted only when card is genuinely lifting.

focus.$description: Single-ring focus indicator — fine for surfaces where the button background is NOT the spring-green accent. For accent-bg surfaces (primary intent), use shadow.focus.dual instead (Atlassian 2024 pattern). v0.11.13 — colour references the spring-green alpha primitive.

focus.dual.$description: v0.9 — Dual-ring focus indicator for accent surfaces. Inner 2 px neutral ring separates the focus halo from the button so the outer ring maintains 3:1 contrast against the surface (WCAG 2.4.13). Atlassian's 2024 fix — needed because a colored ring on a same-colored surface fails the 3:1 floor.

inner.$description: Inner separator ring — paints the page canvas color, creating a 2 px gap between the button and the outer accent ring.

outer.$description: Outer 2 px accent ring (4 px - 2 px inner = 2 px visible). Maintains 3:1 against canvas regardless of button surface. Compose: shadow-focus-dual = inset inner + outer.

stack.$description: v0.9 — composed dual-ring (inner + outer). Apply as a single box-shadow on focus-visible. Note: the var() refs above are the published runtime CSS-var names so both designers and engineers can render this composed value identically; the underlying source-of-truth is color.surface.page (inner) and color.accent.500 (outer).

button.$description: v0.9 — primary-button glow ladder. Three-state ambient halo: rest → hover → active. Reserved exclusively for primary intent (the spring-green CTA). Other intents and surfaces ship zero glow. v0.11.13 — colours migrated from inline lime rgba(74,222,128,X) to the spring-green {color.alpha.accent.*} primitives so the brand recolor cascades.

rest.$description: Default ambient halo on a primary CTA. Soft and steady; signals 'live' without competing with hover.

hover.$description: Hover halo — wider blur + higher alpha. The Glassmorphism reference's 20→30 doubling, scaled for operator density.

active.$description: Press halo — collapsed blur, dimmer alpha. Visual weight ducks momentarily on press, paired with filter: brightness(0.92) — no transform, no scale.

ai-shimmer.$description: v0.9 — AI-action variant idle border (1 px accent at 32% alpha). Animated via CSS keyframe (1.6 s ease-in-out infinite, paused on hover). See globals.css `.lumen-btn-ai`.

accent-glow.$description: Optional outer glow under primary CTAs. Warp signature.

input.$description: v0.6 — input field shell shadows. Composed: lit-edge (rest) + focus/error halo (active state). Apply to .lumen-field wrapper, never to the inner <input>. v0.11.13 — focus + success refs to spring-green primitives, error refs to refined v0.11 danger primitive.

lit-edge.$description: 1px lit top edge — steals the glass-pane reflection trick from glassmorphism without committing to full glass. Dark mode only; no-op on light. v0.11.13 — references color.alpha.paper.06.

focus.$description: v0.6 — focus halo on .lumen-field wrapper. Same recipe as shadow.focus, namespaced for inputs so future theming can diverge.

error.$description: v0.6 — error halo. Painted on focus when [data-invalid=true]; replaces (not stacks with) shadow.input.focus. v0.11.13 — colour now references {color.alpha.danger.32} (refined #E5484D) instead of the inlined v0.10 #ef4444.

success.$description: v0.6 — success halo. Reuses the focus recipe; reserved for explicit post-validation success affordances.
